rows.description: A protester or volunteer stays firm on their cause while treating opponents as human and checking facts. Movements lose credibility when they lie or dehumanise.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: admiration

rows.description: A committed volunteer gives so much time that health, work and family suffer, and they feel guilty about slowing down. Sustained service needs limits and shared load.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: guilt

rows.description: An observer sees that a cause needs organisers, quiet workers and those who fund or write, not just the loudest speakers. Recognising varied contributions reduces resentment inside groups.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: resentment

rows.description: A young adult helps with flood or health relief, feeling tired, useful and sometimes overwhelmed. Working within an organised effort keeps help effective and safe.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: relief, tiredness, overwhelm, trust

rows.subtype: Staying safe and lawful in action [Response]
rows.description: An organiser plans for safety, knows their rights and keeps to peaceful methods. They leave if a crowd turns violent, since a good cause does not justify harm.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: calm, trust

rows.subtype: Pressure to protect the institution's name [Receiver]
rows.description: A student who reports harassment or cheating is told it will damage the college's reputation. They feel guilt and fear, and may withdraw the complaint to escape the pressure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: fear, guilt, detachment

rows.description: A person who reports wrongdoing is isolated, gossiped about and labelled a troublemaker. The retaliation is often social and quiet, and support from even one ally matters greatly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 23–26
related mind states: loneliness

rows.subtype: Told to stay quiet at work [Receiver]
rows.description: An employee who finds a safety or ethics problem is advised by superiors to let it go for the company's sake. They feel fear for their job and doubt about their own judgement.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: fear, doubt, trust

rows.description: A person joins a small concealment, such as a fudged number or a missed report, and each step makes the next easier. Guilt is quieted by telling themselves everyone does it and it protects the team.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: guilt, detachment

rows.description: A professional feels loyalty to colleagues and a superior and also knows something is wrong. Both pulls are real, and the fear of being called a traitor often outweighs the sense of duty to those harmed.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22
related mind states: fear
